name: pyvisa
title: PyVISA
description: Use when working with PyVISA - the Python library for controlling measurement instruments over VISA (GPIB, USB, serial/RS-232, TCPIP/Ethernet): ResourceManager, listing/opening resources, read/write/query, VISA attributes and constants, termination characters, timeouts, event handling, the visa shell, backends (pyvisa-py, NI-VISA), and the high-level/low-level API. import pyvisa. Not for the Python stdlib or other instrument-control libraries.
when_to_use: the PyVISA library for instrument control over VISA - opening a ResourceManager, listing/opening resources (GPIB/USB/serial/TCPIP), read/write/query, VISA attributes and constants, termination characters, timeouts, event handling, the visa shell, choosing a backend (pyvisa-py vs NI-VISA), and the high-level/low-level API.
gotchas: Treat every identifier (class/method/attribute name, VISA constant, resource string like 'GPIB0::14::INSTR', enum value) as an exact reference fact - do not invent or paraphrase the API.
These docs track PyVISA's latest version; verify version-sensitive behavior, defaults, and deprecations against the installed pyvisa version.

PyVISA requires a VISA backend - pyvisa-py (pure Python) or a vendor library (NI-VISA, Keysight, etc.). Available resources, attributes, and behavior depend on the backend plus installed instrument drivers, not on PyVISA alone.
Some autodoc API pages are long, structure-light dumps split into parts; use references/INDEX.md or `rg -n "PATTERN" references/*.md` to locate a symbol rather than reading a whole part file.
